indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of the following words are clumsily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A ham proves clumsy when asked to carve the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like the meat to be carved, but it is a verb. 'awkward' tells you to rearrange TO CARVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggerated theatricality, which is synonymous with overdoing a role.

definitions.meaning: read playfully, a box that holds the sounds of speech
the organ in the throat housing the vocal cords

explanation.surface: Something that holds sound is found in the larynx.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx holds the vocal cords that make speech, so it is popularly called by this everyday anatomical name.

clue.text: Hit the notes during rhythmical monologues

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
music is made of notes

explanation.surface: Someone strikes the right notes during spoken rhythmic performances.
explanation.definitionFit: This genre consists of words chanted rhythmically over a beat, essentially rhythmic spoken monologues.

clue.text: Happen to arrive at the mountain route

parts.note: to come to a place is to arrive at it
a pass is a route through mountains

explanation.surface: A traveller hopes to reach the road over the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic idiom meaning to occur or take place, as in biblical phrasing.

indicators.note: read as un-certain: the word for certain is taken out of pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone offers an excuse that pleasure is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' splits as 'un-' (remove) and 'certain', a synonym of SURE, which comes out of PLEASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an excuse or justification offered, as in a plea of ignorance.

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Bible, after Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a mass departure, and it names the Old Testament book following Genesis.
The word means compelled by duty and also grateful for a favour, as in 'I'm much obliged'.

clue.text: Fact it is in early development

indicators.note: in places the word it inside the rearranged letters
development suggests the letters of early grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A truth that is still at an early stage of being worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges EARLY into REALY, and 'in' puts IT inside it; 'is' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Fact and this word both mean what actually exists or is true rather than imagined.

indicators.note: tragically suggests a disaster has scrambled the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A nimble mountain goat suffered a fatal fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragically' tells you to rearrange IBEX FELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe and this word are synonyms for supple and easily bending.

parts.note: air means a person's manner or bearing
a pump is a light slip-on shoe

explanation.surface: Wearing a slipper, someone carries an instrument that inflates things.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for forcing air into tyres or balls is an instrument for inflating things.

parts.note: to hand something is to give it
Bill is a short form of William

explanation.surface: Someone serves William his notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed notice distributed by hand, like a flyer or leaflet.

clue.text: Wig, or just part of single strand?

definitions.meaning: false hair worn on the head
a fragment of one hair, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: A wig or toupee is a piece of false hair, and read literally the words mean a fragment of one strand.

clue.text: Respect less than half the final outcome

indicators.note: less than half asks for the opening three of the seven letters in the word respect

parts.note: ult, short for ultimo, means of the final or last month

explanation.surface: Respect counts for less than half of the final outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than half' keeps RES, three of the seven letters of Respect. ULT abbreviates ultimo, 'last month' in old business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcome and this word are synonyms for what follows from an action or contest.

parts.note: the mythical giant hunter of the constellation wears a belt of three stars

explanation.surface: A giant hunter wears a belt decorated with stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Three bright stars in a row form the belt of the constellation named after the giant hunter of Greek myth.

parts.note: reads as a person inclined to work late, but means someone who tends patients through the night

explanation.surface: Someone who habitually works late hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer who tends patients during night shifts is literally one tending, at work late.

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Mathematical curves coil round one another.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, a locus is the path traced by points meeting a condition; the plural names such lines.

clue.text: Drink enjoyed by hypochondriac one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals that the words are to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a hypochondriac relishes pain that is fake: sham pain

explanation.surface: A hypochondriac's favourite drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A hypochondriac suffers imaginary, sham pain; said aloud it sounds like the sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling wine from France's Champagne region, a celebratory drink.

clue.text: Say German on watch had item found in kitchen

parts.note: e.g. means for example, signalled by say
a timer is a device for watching time

explanation.surface: A German on guard duty had an item found in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sandglass or timer used in kitchens for boiling eggs.

indicators.note: coming to suggests the letters arrive at a new form

explanation.surface: An identical vessel rises to prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' tells you to rearrange SAME SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis means special importance or prominence given to something.

clue.text: Former pupil's remedy not easily understood

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil, with the possessive s
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: An old boy's remedy is hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means unclear or difficult to understand.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Our imprisoned heart (7)': COURAGE is OUR inside CAGE, but no word gives CAGE except 'imprisoned', which would also be the container indicator; clue likely cut short

explanation.definitionFit: The word means plucky and willing, and also a match or sporting competition.

definitions.meaning: read literally, a wide sheet for a big bed

explanation.definitionFit: A large-format serious newspaper, and literally a wide piece of bed linen.

clue.text: Most uninteresting rough ride good man concluded

indicators.note: concluded places the saint at the end of the word
rough suggests the letters are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A bumpy journey ends with a good man arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: DIREST would also fit the definition and the anagram plus saint; only the crossing letters settle which order the letters take.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry means dull, so the superlative is most dull or uninteresting.

clue.text: New books on churchyard having indentations

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books
CHY is an abbreviation for churchyard

explanation.surface: New books are placed on a churchyard with uneven ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Notched means having indentations cut into it, and this adjective describes the same quality.
The word means the way a person holds themselves, and a railway coach.

clue.text: Single night, only part of it, spent in valley

indicators.note: only part of it signals the letters are taken from within the words single night

explanation.surface: A single night was spent in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Assumption that building had not been completed

indicators.note: not completed means the last letter is missing

parts.note: premises are a building and its grounds

explanation.surface: Someone assumes the building work was never finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had not been completed' drops the last letter of PREMISES.
explanation.definitionFit: A premise is a proposition assumed as the basis for an argument.

clue.text: Man first about to return record

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
1st written with I for the digit one

indicators.note: to return signals the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The man comes back first to set a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official record or list.

clue.text: Change one's habit, that's the remedy

definitions.meaning: to dress again, putting on different clothes

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-dress it means changing clothes; as one word it means a remedy for a wrong.
